findings.claim: Task 5's source check reads grid-template-areas through areaRows, which only extracts double-quoted strings (/"([^"]*)"/g). CSS strings may be delimited by either a double quote or an apostrophe, so a correct solution written as grid-template-areas: 'header header' 'main aside' 'footer footer'; renders the required layout but areaRows returns [] and Task 5 fails with 'From 1000px wide, the named regions do not yet form the required page layout.' Pre-existing (areaRows is unchanged and the old deepEqual had the same input); the current JSON.stringify comparison neither causes nor fixes it. Low because the Grid topic page and every MDN example use double quotes, so few learners will hit it.

evidence.section: Executed in scratch copy $TMPDIR/pep-rf2-sme/html-and-css (bytes verified against LAB_BUNDLE.sha256 from pep export-lab; npm ci; node --test --test-reporter=spec): private completion passes 11/11; the same completion with only the area map rewritten in single quotes gives 10 pass / 1 fail, task 5 failing on the named-regions source assertion.

W3C CSS Syntax Module Level 3, 4.3.1 Consume a token and 4.3.5 Consume a string token, retrieved 2026-11-10T06:50:21Z: https://www.w3.org/TR/css-syntax-3/ - both U+0022 QUOTATION MARK and U+0027 APOSTROPHE: 'Consume a string token and return it.'

MDN grid-template-areas, retrieved 2026-11-10T06:50:21Z: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/Reference/Properties/grid-template-areas - formal syntax 'none | <string>+'; no quote type is mandated.

findings.recommendation: Let areaRows accept either delimiter, for example /(["'])(.*?)\1/g taking the second group, and add a single-quoted area map to the solved-run variants. Alternatively state double quotes in README Task 5 Hint 2.
